title: What If Every Car in America Went Electric Tomorrow? #shorts

scenes.text: What if every car in America went electric tomorrow? Could the power grid survive?
Americans drive over three trillion miles a year. That's about a thousand terawatt hours of electricity.
Last year the whole country made a record of about four thousand four hundred. So we need about a fifth more.
The twist? Most cars charge at night, when power plants are idle. A national lab found that spare power could charge most of our cars.
The real weak spot is your street. One fast charging car can pull as much as fifty homes.
So the energy exists. Just not at six p.m. Would you charge at night? Follow EV Drive.
